children: Gold futures fell to the lowest in more than a year on Friday and silver slipped below $50/oz for the first time ​since last November, as wars in the Middle East and Russia-Ukraine push oil prices higher, raising inflation concerns with implications of higher interest rates.
Crude oil prices jumped more than 2% following another tanker attack in the Strait of Hormuz, adding to inflation worries and expectations that U.S. Federal Reserve policy will remain restrictive.
Data on Thursday showed U.S. ‌inflation accelerated in September as consumers paid more for gasoline and ‌other goods, buttressing economists' expectations of a rate hike in December.

The Fed held its benchmark rate steady at 3.75%-4% and the European Central Bank also held rates steady this week, although both central banks warned that more expensive energy could push inflation higher.

"Even though holds were delivered by major central ​banks this week, the indication was that the higher-for-longer theme prevails, and that's weighing on precious metals," according to Peter Grant, VP and senior metals strategist at Zaner Metals.

Another factor behind the swoon in precious metals may have been the day's sharp decline in tech stocks, with the tech-heavy Masdaq plunging nearly 3%, which may have led to forced selling and margin ⁠calls.

The selloff could be "partly emanating from the crypto hack, which is triggering a flight to cash and putting additional selling pressure on the metals," Peter Cardillo of Spartan Capital said in a note.

sank 5.9% to $49.097/oz, its lowest close since November 7.
For the full week, gold and silver declined 2.7% and 8.6%, respectively.
